code.title: Your settings, in code
code.sub: What you pick next to the chat, as you would write it. The colours are n8n's own variables, so a page styled for n8n's widget keeps its look.
cards.title: Answers with cards
cards.lead: n8n's chat carries only text, so a card travels as text: a code block whose language names the card, holding its fields as JSON, after the sentence that answers. This widget draws it; n8n's own chat shows the sentence and the code.
cards.how: Build the block in a Code node from your tool's real result rather than asking the model to write JSON: it is exact every time. The workflows below do it behind a richCards setting.
cards.list: Ready-made: order (bookings too), product, place, items, stats and more, each loaded the first time an answer uses it. Their fields.
cards.own.title: Your own card
cards.own.lead: A support ticket, a delivery slot, a loyalty balance: define it once, and your workflow sends it like the others. Here is a ticket card, drawn live below by the code beside it.
yours.title: Try it with your n8n
yours.lead: Paste your Chat Trigger's production URL: the chat above switches to your workflow. The URL stays in your browser; this site never sees your conversation.
yours.ok: Connected: the chat above now talks to your workflow.
yours.err.url: That is not a URL. Use the Chat Trigger's production URL, the one that ends in /chat.
yours.err.cors: Your n8n refused this site, or cannot be reached. In the Chat Trigger, add https://n8n-chat.apartejs.dev to Allowed Origins (CORS), and check the URL.
yours.err.404: Your n8n answered 404: activate the workflow, and turn on Make Chat Publicly Available in the Chat Trigger.
yours.err.local: A localhost n8n: your browser may ask to allow access to your local network. If it blocks it, use a public URL (n8n Cloud, a tunnel).
yours.err.other: Your n8n answered {status}. Check the Chat Trigger's settings.
yours.need: You need: an active workflow, a Chat Trigger with Make Chat Publicly Available on, and this site in its Allowed Origins (the default * allows it).

wf.shop.title: Shop assistant
wf.shop.text: Products, orders and returns: a product question answered with its card (price, sizes, stock), an order told only to its email, only a shipped order in its return window goes back, a photo for a damaged item, a confirmation with buttons, an email to your support.
wf.booking.title: Booking assistant
wf.booking.text: Free times from your opening hours, a name and an email, a confirmation with buttons, a last check that the time is still free, the booking saved in a Data Table, and your address and hours on a card.
wf.docs.title: Questions about a document
wf.docs.text: The visitor attaches a PDF or a text file and asks about it; the answers stay on the document. Works with n8n's own chat too.
aparte.title: Made with aparté, open to all of it
aparte.lead: The widget is built with aparté, an open-source library for AI chats. Its setup option hands you aparté's config: the plugins that draw an answer (maths, diagrams, charts, cards of your own) work in your n8n chat, in one line each.
aparte.markdown.text: Lists, tables, links and highlighted code in every answer. Built in.
aparte.cards.text: Ready-made and your own, from a code block in the answer. Built in.
aparte.buttons.text: A Chat node that waits for an approval asks with buttons. Built in.
aparte.charts.text: From a code block, with ECharts or Chart.js: @aparte/plugin-echarts, @aparte/plugin-chartjs.
why.title: Why switch from n8n's widget
why.sub: Same options, same Chat Trigger, same session in the browser. Measured on 31 October 2026 against @n8n/chat 1.44.7.
why.languages.ours: ten, loaded one at a time
why.embedded: In the page, not in a corner
install.title: Install
install.sub: Coming from @n8n/chat: change the two URLs. Everything else carries over.
install.npm: Or from npm: npm install @aparte/n8n-chat. Every option is in the README.

wfp.shop.req:
• An n8n your visitors' browsers can reach on a public URL, with data tables (tested on n8n 2.45.7).
  • A chat model that can call tools: an OpenAI key, or any model n8n supports.
  • An SMTP account to email your support team, or swap that node for Gmail, Outlook or Slack.
wfp.shop.steps:
• Import the JSON into n8n.
  • In Settings: your shop's name, your support and sender addresses. Leave richCards on for this widget.
  • Set your currency in Settings, and connect your products: replace Find products with a WooCommerce Tool (Product → Get Many).
  • Add your credentials to Chat model and Tell support, connect your orders (the note under the workflow shows where), and set the return window in Return policy.
  • In When chat message received: your site in Allowed Origins. Publish, and copy the production URL that ends in /chat.
  • Paste the widget in your page, with that URL:
wfp.booking.req:
• An n8n your visitors' browsers can reach on a public URL, with data tables (tested on n8n 2.45.7).
  • A chat model that can call tools: an OpenAI key, or any model n8n supports.
wfp.booking.steps:
• Import the JSON into n8n.
  • In Settings: your business name, the service, the timezone, your opening days and hours, the length of an appointment. Leave richCards on for this widget.
  • Put your address and phone number in Settings: they are on the card when a visitor asks where you are.
  • Add your credentials to Chat model.
  • In When chat message received: your site in Allowed Origins. Publish, and copy the production URL that ends in /chat.
  • Paste the widget in your page, with that URL:

basics.buttons.title: Buttons from a Chat node

basics.buttons.greeting: Write anything: this workflow answers with a question and two buttons.
basics.buttons.how: In n8n: a Chat node set to Send and Wait for Response, approval type, on a Chat Trigger answering through response nodes.
basics.markdown.title: Markdown, tables and code

basics.markdown.how: Nothing to set: the workflow's answer is Markdown, the widget draws it.
basics.files.title: Files the visitor attaches
basics.files.text: Pictures and PDFs, picked, dropped or pasted; your workflow receives them as n8n's widget sends them. Try one: the workflow says what it received.
basics.files.greeting: Attach a picture or a PDF with the paperclip.
basics.errors.title: An error the visitor can read
basics.errors.text: When the workflow fails, the visitor reads a plain sentence in their language, not n8n's raw message; the details go to the page's console.
basics.errors.greeting: Send anything: this workflow fails on purpose.
basics.errors.how: Nothing to set. The workflow's own error message stays on the console for you.
